reference.pathophysiology: Autoimmune plaques strip central myelin in time and space producing relapsing optic, brainstem, spinal and cerebellar syndromes; NMO attacks aquaporin-rich optic nerves and cord longitudinally, and MOGAD favours bilateral optic nerves in children.
additionalDifferentials: MS versus NMO versus MOGAD versus ADEM by AQP4 MOG and lesion length
Relapse versus progressive by recovery and baseline
INO versus myasthenia by adduction and fatiguability
